title: Has a leap second ever been taken away?

scenes.purpose: Ground the answer in the written record itself before the narration resolves it.

visual.description: Two tiles side by side, joined by a single rising line. The left tile reads 1972 / 10 s; the right tile reads 2017 / 37 s. The line draws from left to right as the narration crosses from '10 seconds' to '37 seconds', climbing in even steps and never dipping; the right tile brightens to the accent once the line reaches it.

chart.title: TAI minus UTC
chart.note: The table's value only ever rises between these tiles; it never falls.

scenes.direction: Cut to the two tiles; the connecting line draws left to right as the narration crosses from '10 seconds' to '37 seconds'.
scenes.narration: The official table of TAI-UTC runs from 10 seconds in 1972 to 37 seconds in 2017, climbing by exactly one second at every entry.

scenes.purpose: State the resolution plainly: every step the record shows went one way.

visual.description: Dark field; the line types on in large serif, centred. On the word 'taken away' the text holds and turns to the glow.
onScreenText: Added every time. Never taken away.

scenes.direction: Hard cut from the tiles to the statement; hold half a second after it settles.
scenes.narration: Every leap second since civil time started using them has been added, and none has ever been taken away.
